leader.name: Konrad Voss
leader.title: Reichskanzler
leader.biography: A former signals officer and party organiser, Voss consolidated the nationalist bloc after the 1933 emergency decrees. He governs through a cabinet of technocrats and soldiers, and has made rearmament the central project of the state.

traits.name: Consolidated Rule
traits.description: The cabinet answers to the chancellery, not the Reichstag.

traits.name: Distrust of Moscow
traits.description: Diplomatic relations with the Soviet Union are permanently strained.

parties.name: National Unity Front
parties.description: The governing movement: a coalition of nationalist associations, ex-officers and industrial interest groups.

parties.name: Social Democratic Party
parties.description: The largest opposition bloc, reduced but still rooted in the industrial cities and trade unions.

parties.name: Communist Party
parties.description: Operating semi-legally through factory cells and front organisations.

parties.name: Centre Party
parties.description: Catholic regional politics, cautious of both the government and the far left.

advisors.name: Walther Kleist
advisors.description: A career diplomat from the eastern service who argues that German security lies in a continental bloc of small states.

advisors.name: Ilse Brandt
advisors.description: Minister of propaganda and public welfare. Her organisation reaches every town hall and factory floor.

advisors.name: Gen. Otto Reinecke
advisors.description: The army's chief planner, credited with the mobilisation schedule that underpins the rearmament programme.

advisors.name: Erich Falk
advisors.description: Runs the Abwehr's foreign section. His networks in Prague and Warsaw are considered the best in Europe.

advisors.name: Prof. Hans Arndt
advisors.description: Professor of operational science at the war academy and an unapologetic advocate of fast, mechanised campaigns.

modifiers.name: Reichsbank Credit Programme
modifiers.description: Short-term treasury notes finance the defence programme; the machinery works, but it is not sustainable forever.

modifiers.name: Dual Alliance Clause
modifiers.description: Standing commitments to a southern ally keep the general staff planning for two fronts.

modifiers.name: Fuel Shortage
modifiers.description: Domestic oil fields cover a fraction of demand. Every mechanised division is tied to imports.

decisions.name: National Labour Service
decisions.description: Extend the compulsory labour service to build roads, drain marshes and bring new land into cultivation.

decisions.name: Motorway Programme
decisions.description: Authorise the first sections of the north-south motorway scheme. It will take years to pay back, but the construction ministry insists it will.

decisions.name: Expand the Officer Corps
decisions.description: Open three new cadet academies and recall retired officers to the training establishment.

decisions.name: Trade Mission to the Balkans
decisions.description: Send a commercial delegation to Bucharest and Belgrade to secure grain, oil and chrome in exchange for machinery and machine tools.

decisions.name: National Housing Programme
decisions.description: Fund a public housing drive in the industrial cities to ease overcrowding and quiet criticism of the government.

decisions.name: Requisition Civilian Industry
decisions.description: Convert consumer plants to military contracts. Popularity will suffer, but the field army needs the capacity now.

agency.name: Abwehr
agency.description: The unified military intelligence service, with stations in every European capital and a growing cipher bureau.
